# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
**Scope:** Migrate 40,000 existing users from legacy billing system ("Old") to new billing system ("New"). Both systems run in parallel throughout the rollout.

## Overview

The migration moves users in three increasing-size batches, validating financial correctness and system stability at each step before proceeding. Old and New run concurrently for the entire rollout; Old is kept fully operational as a fallback until well after 100% of users are migrated and a separate post-migration stabilization period has passed.

---

## Phase 1: Canary
**Users:** 1% (~400 users)
**Entry criterion:** New system has passed a full end-to-end billing cycle (invoice generation, payment capture, refund, and dunning) in staging with zero data-integrity errors, and rollback tooling to revert a user to Old has been tested successfully at least once.

**Cohort selection:** Internal/employee accounts and opted-in low-risk test customers (non-enterprise, monthly plans, no active disputes).

**Duration:** Minimum 5 business days, spanning at least one full billing cycle for the cohort.

**Actions:**
- Enable dual-write shadow mode (New processes transactions; Old remains system of record) for 48 hours before cutting any user's system-of-record over.
- Cut over the 1% cohort to New as system of record.
- Reconcile every transaction between Old and New daily.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopters
**Users:** 15% (~6,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with the halt metric (below) never breached, invoice/payment discrepancy rate ≤0.1% for the Phase 1 cohort, zero P1/P2 incidents attributed to New, and support ticket volume for migrated users within 1.2x of the baseline rate for non-migrated users.

**Cohort selection:** Broader mix of plan types and geographies, but excluding enterprise accounts with custom contracts and any account with an active billing dispute.

**Duration:** Minimum 7 business days.

**Actions:**
- Migrate in 3 sub-batches of 5% each, 48 hours apart, re-checking the halt metric before each sub-batch.
- Continue daily reconciliation; add automated variance alerting.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (Full Migration)
**Users:** 84% (~33,600 users), including enterprise/custom-contract accounts last
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed in full with the halt metric never breached, discrepancy rate ≤0.05%, finance team has signed off on reconciliation reports for Phases 1–2, and a dedicated incident-response rotation is staffed for the duration of Phase 3.

**Cohort selection:** All remaining users, migrated in waves by segment (SMB → mid-market → enterprise), enterprise accounts migrated last and individually validated with their assigned account manager before cutover.

**Duration:** Minimum 10 business days, with enterprise accounts migrated no faster than 1 wave every 2 business days.

**Actions:**
- Migrate remaining users in waves of no more than 10% of total user base per day.
- Enterprise/custom-contract accounts get a manual pre-migration billing reconciliation review before cutover.
- Old system remains fully operational, receiving no new signups but able to process/service any user rolled back to it.

**Note:** Decommissioning, disabling, or deleting the Old system is explicitly **out of scope for Phase 3** and for the final migration batch. It is handled in a separate, subsequent Phase 4 (Old System Retirement) that begins only after a minimum 30-day parallel-run stabilization period post-100%-migration, a final audit reconciliation, and explicit sign-off from Finance and Legal/Compliance (for record retention requirements).

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

Any of the following automatically pauses the rollout (no further users migrated) and triggers incident review before resuming:

- **Billing discrepancy rate > 0.5%** of transactions in any 24-hour window for migrated users (transaction amount, currency, or status mismatch between Old and New reconciliation).
- **Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds baseline (Old system) failure rate by more than 25% relative**, measured over a rolling 6-hour window.
- **P1 incident** (customer-facing billing outage, duplicate charges, or failed charge capture affecting >50 users) attributed to New at any point.
- **Support ticket volume from migrated users exceeds 2x the pre-migration baseline** for that cohort over any 24-hour window.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double charges occur when both systems briefly consider themselves system of record for the same user | Enforce a single-writer flag per user account gated by a distributed lock; run dual-write in shadow (read-only compare) mode for 48 hours before any cutover | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Data mapping errors (e.g., tax rules, currency, proration logic) cause silent under- or over-billing that isn't caught until customer complaints arrive | Automated daily reconciliation job comparing Old vs. New computed amounts per invoice, with alerting on any variance above threshold | Billing Data/QA Lead
RISK: Rollback of a migrated user back to Old is incomplete, leaving orphaned payment methods or subscription state in New | Build and test an automated rollback script per migration phase; require a successful rollback dry-run as an entry criterion for Phase 2 | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated with incorrect pricing, damaging a high-value relationship | Migrate enterprise accounts last, individually, with manual reconciliation review and account manager sign-off before cutover | Enterprise Account Management Lead
RISK: Migration coincides with a customer's billing cycle boundary, causing missed or duplicate invoice generation | Freeze migrations for any account within 48 hours of its scheduled invoice date; reschedule to the next available window | Billing Operations Lead

PHASES: 3
